clue.text: Chat's dropped at change of service provider?

indicators.note: Chat's dropped means Chat has had the following word let fall out of it

parts.note: a chat is an informal conversation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumble about switching phone or internet supplier and losing your chat connection.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'service provider' is not a phone company but a church: a convert changes which religious services they attend.
explanation.definitionFit: Conversion is the act of changing one's religion, so moving to a different provider of worship services.

clue.text: Police beginning to excavate wooded area

parts.note: cops is slang for the police

indicators.note: beginning to a word means only its opening letter is used

parts.note: supplies its first letter

explanation.surface: Officers start digging up a patch of woodland, as at a crime scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small thicket or group of trees, a little wooded area.

clue.text: One included among eminent women to manage rearing?

definitions.text: One included among eminent women to manage rearing?

indicators.note: rearing up, in a down entry, means the whole string is read from bottom to top
included among means the one letter goes inside the women's word

parts.note: dames are women honoured with the British title equivalent to a knighthood
the Roman numeral for one
to run something is to manage it

explanation.surface: A woman counted among the great and good, helping bring up children.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a nanny is one who manages the rearing of children.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid is a woman employed to look after young children, managing their upbringing.

clue.text: Band showing promise in battle arena

parts.note: an engagement is a military encounter, a battle
a ring is an arena, as for boxing or the circus

explanation.surface: A musical group shows potential in a combat venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians, but it is a ring worn on the finger; 'promise' is a promise to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: An engagement ring is a finger band given as a token of a promise of marriage.

clue.text: Because note is not fake

parts.note: since can mean because, as in 'since you ask'
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A justification that a written note is genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere means genuine and honest, the opposite of a feigned or put-on manner.

clue.text: Crime of hot stuff dealer

parts.note: taken as written
a fence is a dealer in stolen goods, which are called hot

explanation.surface: Describing the illegal trade of someone selling stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' here is criminal slang for stolen, not spicy or attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence is a breach of the law, a crime.

clue.text: Comeback of Friends is a hit

indicators.note: a comeback here is a coming back, so the word for friends is read backwards

parts.note: pals are friends

explanation.surface: The return of the TV sitcom Friends proves a success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friends' and 'hit' suggest the sitcom and its ratings; the hit is a smack.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap is a blow with the open hand, a hit.

clue.text: Morning everyone — on the way up, I'll carry your bags

indicators.note: on the way up, in a down entry, means the letters climb from bottom to top

parts.note: am stands for morning, ante meridiem
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A cheery hotel porter greets guests and offers to take their luggage upstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The porter talking is really an Andean pack animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Llamas are used as pack animals in South America, carrying loads for people.

clue.text: I maintain chair is mine

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who professes or maintains, read as an agent noun
second meaning: a university ... holds a chair

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer into a verb meaning maintain plus the agent ending; the second is the academic.
explanation.definitionFit: A professor holds a named chair, the senior teaching post in a university department.

clue.text: Peevish employer's report that may provide access to other work

definitions.text: that may provide access to other work

parts.note: cross means irritable or peevish
a reference is a report on a worker written by an employer

explanation.surface: An irritable boss writes a reference that might help someone get another job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Other work' looks like another job; it is another part of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-reference directs the reader to another passage or entry elsewhere in the text.

clue.text: Model soldier absent without leave at last

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: without here means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: gone means away, absent

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of leave

parts.note: supplies its last letter

explanation.surface: A perfect soldier who has gone AWOL.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absent without leave' looks like the military phrase AWOL; it splits into three separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a model of excellence, a perfect example.

clue.text: Disorder a long way in the past involving Republican

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the party letter goes inside

parts.note: far means a long way
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: Political chaos in some distant era with a Republican involved.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused mixture or jumble, a muddle.

clue.text: Holding on to leaflets, refusing to abandon environmentalist politics?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: keeping leaves all year round, as a tree does
second meaning, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaflets' suggests campaign flyers; it means little leaves. The second sense splits the answer into always plus the Green party.
explanation.definitionFit: Evergreen plants retain their foliage through every season instead of shedding it in autumn.

clue.text: Small step — taken after journey here?

parts.note: a pace is a single step

explanation.surface: Neil Armstrong's small step, taken after the long trip to the Moon.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Armstrong's 'one small step' on the Moon in 1969.
explanation.definitionFit: Outer space is where an astronaut takes that famous step after the journey from Earth.

clue.text: Chuck maiden in abyss

parts.note: Chuck and Chas are both short forms of Charles
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Throw a young woman into a bottomless pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck' reads as throw; it is a name, a pet form of Charles.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasm is a deep gorge or fissure, an abyss.

clue.text: Take your chances with fish I deem dodgy!

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the anagram fodder
taken as written, the rest of the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An angler's dare to gamble on a fish one suspects.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpe diem is Latin for seize the day, urging one to grab opportunities.

clue.text: Denounces amount paid to bosses?

parts.note: exec is short for executive, a boss
rates are amounts charged or paid

explanation.surface: Workers complain about what the bosses are paid.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, the bosses earn the 'exec rates'.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to curse or condemn loudly, to denounce.

clue.text: Barber's lotion, as blended with essence of myrrh

indicators.note: blended means mixed together, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the anagram fodder
taken as written, joining the anagram fodder

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its central letter

parts.note: supplies its middle letter

explanation.surface: A hairdresser's lotion mixed with a myrrh extract.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonsorial means relating to hairdressing or to barbers and their work.

clue.text: Unemployed joiner from Munich getting into Socialist Worker?

indicators.note: getting into means the German word goes inside the others

parts.note: red is a common term for a left-winger
an ant is the standard crossword worker
und is German for and, a joining word

explanation.surface: A German carpenter out of work joins the Socialist Worker party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiner' suggests a carpenter; it is a conjunction, a word that joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone made redundant has lost their job because it is no longer needed.

clue.text: Mean, fit dogs hail from Rome

indicators.note: dogs means follows, so the temper word comes after the greeting

parts.note: ave is the Latin greeting, hail
a rage is a fit of temper

explanation.surface: Healthy hounds greet you in Latin, though nastily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dogs' looks like animals; it is a verb meaning follows closely.
explanation.definitionFit: The average is the arithmetic mean of a set of numbers.

clue.text: Do pleat, knitting jumper for the future?

indicators.note: knitting means working the letters together into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, part of the anagram fodder
taken as written, the rest of the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Instructions for knitting a pleated sweater to wear later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like a British sweater, as the knitting suggests; it is a future frog.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is a frog larva, which will grow into a leaping amphibian.

clue.text: More thinly sliced piece of fish, waiter, without delay!

parts.note: a fin is part of a fish

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a word is removed

parts.note: taken as written
to wait is to delay

explanation.surface: A diner urges the waiter to bring thinner slices of fish at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Finer can mean thinner or more delicate, as in finer slices.

clue.text: Boob fear after losing leader

indicators.note: after losing its leader the word drops its first letter

parts.note: terror is extreme fear

explanation.surface: Anxiety about a wardrobe malfunction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boob' is informal British for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is a foolish mistake, a blunder.

clue.text: No cap for toy gun

indicators.note: no cap means the word loses its top letter in this down entry

parts.note: to trifle with something is to toy with it

explanation.surface: A toy gun sold without its caps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cap' suggests the noise caps of a toy gun; it means the top letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled firearm, a gun.

clue.text: "Will this do for duvet day?" I wondered blearily

definitions.text: Will this do for duvet day?

indicators.note: blearily means with unfocused eyes, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone half-awake wonders whether to take a lazy day in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: A duvet day is British slang for a day off spent at home, typically in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt filled with down, so it would serve as a duvet.

clue.text: Queen coming up short in African country

indicators.note: coming up, in a down entry, means read from bottom to top
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: regina is Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A monarch rising briefly to power in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked nation in West Africa.

clue.text: Royal lover infiltrating internal area

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so the lover goes within

parts.note: a fan is a devotee or lover of something

explanation.surface: A royal's paramour slips into the private quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: An infanta is a daughter of the Spanish or Portuguese monarch, a princess.

clue.text: Taking regular bites from onion, Henry VIII perhaps making a pig of himself?

indicators.note: regular bites take every other letter of the word

parts.note: its first, third and fifth letters are the regular bites
Henry VIII is one example of a king

explanation.surface: Henry VIII gorging on onions at a banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is literal: a pig is made by grunting like one.
explanation.definitionFit: Oinking is the grunting sound a pig makes, so imitating a pig.

clue.text: Fake email going round, ensnaring humble folk with promise of vast inheritance?

definitions.text: humble folk with promise of vast inheritance?

indicators.note: going round means turning back, so the letters run right to left
ensnaring means trapping the letters within the words

parts.note: the run of letters held in these words

explanation.surface: A scam email promising a fortune lures in gullible people.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition recalls the Beatitude 'Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth'.
explanation.definitionFit: The meek are the gentle and humble, promised the earth as their inheritance in the Gospel.

clue.text: Brainy, brewing beer in basement

indicators.note: in means placed inside the basement word

parts.note: a cellar is a basement

indicators.note: brewing means being worked up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A clever home-brewer making beer in the cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerebellar relates to the cerebellum, a part of the brain, so literally brain-related.
